full_judgment:
Mr. Faruque Ahmed, J: This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner was issued directing the defendant-opposite parties 1 & 2 to show cause as to why the order dated 22.2.88 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Jessore in Miscellaneous Judicial Case No. 8 of 1987 should not be set aside and or such other or further order or orders as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

 2. The plaintiff-petitioners filed an application on 14.1.87 under Order 9 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Judicial Case No. 8 of 1987 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Jessore alleging inter alia, that the exparte judgment and order dated 17.12.86 dismissing Title Suit No. 92 of 1979 was passed because of the absence of the plaintiff-petitioner who is an old man was seriously ill and bed-ridden, and got treatment in Koloroa Hospital and that sons and other relatives of the petitioner being seriously engaged for the treatment of the petitioner they could not take any step on 17.12.86. t he date fixed for hearing of the suit and as a result the suit was dismissed for default. 

 3. The learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and order dated 25.1.88 allowed the said Miscellaneous Case with direction that the petitioner was to pay Tk. 300/- as cost by 22.2.88, in default, the application shall be deemed to have been disallowed. 

 10. It appears that the learned trial Court allowed the Miscellaneous case for restoration of Title Suit No. 92 of 1979 with a condition that the plaintiff was to deposit Tk. 300/- as cost by 22.2.88 in default, the Miscellaneous Case shall be treated as dismissed. 

 12. It also appears that the learned trial Court gave the last date for depositing the cost upto 22.2.88 and on that date the plaintiff-petitioner prayed for extension of time to deposit the cost and that the day being the last day, the learned Court was fully competent to consider the application for extension of time as the learned trial Court was in seisin of the matter till that day. The conditional order dated 25.1.88 shows that unless the petitioner would deposit the money by 22.2.88 the case should be deemed to have been dismissed which indicates that the order has not become final till expiry of 22.2.88 of cause, after expiry of 22.2.88 the position would have been different. Since the petitioner applied for extension of time on 22.2.88 which was within the given time, the learned Court under the facts and circumstances of the case and also under Section 148 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure could extend the time for deposit of the cost. This view finds support in the case of Afazuddin VS. Abdur Rahman Shaikh reported in 11 DLR 23 and Shaikh Ayezuddin Vs. Priya Shankar Chowdhury reported in 6 DLR 595.
